quotes.text: Contract reference: DDS-2025-118
THIS CONTRACT is made between NORTHGATE PETROLEUM OPERATING COMPANY ("the Company") and MERIDIAN DOWNHOLE SERVICES LTD ("the Contractor")

Each well is called off by a written notice stating the well name, the rig, the field and the well class. The well class stated in the call-off governs the whole well and is not revised while the well is drilled.
The Contractor shall invoice each well separately, for a period of consecutive days on the well.
A well is HPHT where the call-off so states; the class-rated factor applies to the whole well and not only to the deeper sections.
A well is Extended Reach where the call-off so states, whatever the horizontal displacement achieved.

discrepancies: Note (not a discrepancy): on p1 the contract reference and the Contractor's name are in the opening text above the particulars table, not in the table itself; the table holds dates, currency, VAT, rounding, invoicing and operations. The validation cases (near-miss references DSS-2025-118 / DDS-2025-181; line well differing from header well) are consistent with the printed reference DDS-2025-118 and Cl.32 'invoice each well separately'; the contract does not itself say how such mismatches are to be recorded.

quotes.text: The Contractor shall invoice each well separately, for a period of consecutive days on the well. Every charge on an invoice is for a day within the period the invoice states.
Each charge states the date, the service code, the description, the hole section, the status of the day, the quantity, the unit, the rate and the amount
stated as a single charge under code DS-900 with a negative amount.

discrepancies: Note on the validation case (ambiguity, not resolved): Cl.32 says every charge is for a day within the period and Cl.34 says each charge states the date, while Cl.36 and Cl.38 call the DS-900 discount a 'charge' ("the discount charge under Clause 38"; "a single charge under code DS-900"). The text does not say whether the DS-900 discount charge must carry a date, nor does p8 itself say a blank DS-900 date is not a missing report; that conclusion rests on Cl.37 (documents only for services Schedule 5 lists), which is on p8 but not cited in this rule's sources.

quotes.text: Commencement date 01 January 2025
Expiry date 31 December 2025
The Term as let ran from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025. As twice extended it runs from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2026.

The Expiry Date stated in the Form of Agreement is extended to 30 June 2026 (extension of the Term, 181 days). The Commencement Date is unchanged. Services performed on or before the extended Expiry Date are chargeable under this Contract; services performed after it are not.

The Expiry Date stated in the Form of Agreement is extended to 31 December 2026 (second extension of the Term, 184 days). The Commencement Date is unchanged. Services performed on or before the extended Expiry Date are chargeable under this Contract; services performed after it are not.
An invoice shall not be submitted before the last day of its period and shall be submitted within 30 days after it.

discrepancies: Note (not a discrepancy): the text says 'within 30 days after it' without saying how the days are counted; the validation reading (day 30 after the last day inside, day 31 outside) is consistent with it. Submission on the last day of the period itself is not barred ('shall not be submitted before the last day').

quotes.text: A Daily Drilling Report shall be issued for every day on which the Contractor is on the well.
It is signed by the Company Representative and the Contractor's lead directional driller.
A charge for a service Schedule 5 lists is not payable until the document Schedule 5 names has been delivered for the day or run the charge is for.
The status of the day is recorded by the Company Representative and is final for the purposes of Clause 19.
A report may be corrected only by a revision signed by both signatories before the invoice for the day is submitted.

One Daily Drilling Report is issued for each well and day (Clause 19). It carries the operations summary and, as numbered parts, every other record this Contract makes a condition of payment. There are no separate run, survey, source or loss documents.
B BHA run record: run number, first and last day of the run, tools in the run, circulating hours, metres logged and reamed, and whether a radioactive source was carried every day of a run

A charge for a service below is not payable until the part named has been completed in the Daily Drilling Report for the day or run the charge is for (Clause 37). A part that does not apply to the day is omitted; a part that applies and is absent is a record not delivered.
Each Daily Drilling Report bears a number in the series DDR, and that number is quoted against every line of that day on the invoice.

discrepancies: Notes (ambiguities, not resolved): (1) Cl.16 (p5, not cited) provides for a separate BHA Run Report, Gyro Survey Report, Source Handling Certificate and Lost in Hole Report, while Sch 5 (p24) says 'There are no separate run, survey, source or loss documents'; the rule follows Sch 5 (Cl.2 on p3: 'A Schedule prevails over a Part'). R9 (p14) also still refers to a BHA Run Report. (2) Cl.37/Sch 5 make only the listed codes (DD-111, DD-130, LW-410 to LW-413, LW-420, RM-510, LH-711 to LH-714) conditional on a completed part; the text does not expressly make the DDR itself, or its signatures, a condition of payment for other service lines, although Cl.15 requires the report and its two signatures and 19A requires the DDR number against every line of the day. (3) Sch 5 refers to 'Clause 19' for the daily report, whereas the report clause on p5 is Clause 15. (4) The validation cases 'placeholder signature' and 'report number of another day (mismatch, not duplicate)' are readings of Cl.15 and 19A; the text does not use those terms.

quotes.text: The Daily Drilling Report is written in the ordinary words of the rig (Clause 19A). The terms below are the ones it uses for the items Schedule 1 prices.
DD-102 Directional coordinator, office based night man
HC-640 Cuttings bed monitoring float sub
LH-714 Lost in hole, LWD resistivity tool gamma tool
LW-410 LWD resistivity, logged gamma tool
A tool lost in the hole is recorded by the term above; the item charged is the replacement value Schedule 6 states against it.
The report is written by the Contractor's supervisor in the ordinary words of the rig and does not repeat the descriptions in Schedule 1 or carry the service codes.
Personnel are charged per person-day for the persons recorded on the rig on the Daily Drilling Report.
A rental charged by the day is charged for a day only where the Daily Drilling Report records the tool in the hole on that day.
the failed tool is charged only on days the report records it in the hole.
A person on a crew change day is counted once, whether arriving or departing.
What each service covers and the event its charge is for. Item DD-102 is office based and is charged per day for each coordinator the Daily Drilling Report records.
DD-101 Directional driller, 24-hour coverage each person recorded on the rig on the Daily Drilling Report, per day
HC-640 Cuttings bed monitoring each day the Daily Drilling Report records the tool in the hole

discrepancies: Notes (ambiguities, not resolved): (1) 19A (p35) says the report does not carry the service codes, while R5 and R6 (p14, not cited) say the report lists rental tools and personnel 'by service code'. (2) Sch 8 (p27) is internally inconsistent for DD-102: the lead-in says it is charged per day for each coordinator the report records, but the table row says 'each day the Daily Drilling Report records the tool in the hole'. (3) Appendix G gives the same report term to more than one code ('gamma tool' for LW-410 and LH-714; 'mud motor' for DD-110 and LH-711; 'rotary steerable' for DD-120 and LH-712; 'MWD collar' for MW-310 and LH-713), and its terms do not follow the Schedule 1 descriptions (e.g. LW-411 density and neutron = 'resistivity tool', LW-412 sonic = 'density-neutron', MW-310 'MWD directional and gamma tool' = 'MWD collar'). The validation mappings ('night man' -> DD-102, 'gamma tool' -> LW-410 or LH-714 in a loss context, 'float sub' -> HC-640) match the printed table; the separation of LW-410 from LH-714 by loss context rests on the p36 footnote.

quotes.text: Item DD-120 is charged per circulating hour recorded on the Daily Drilling Report for an Operating day, subject to a minimum of 6 hours on any Operating day on which the tool is in the hole.
Item PD-210 is charged for the metres drilled on the day, taken from the measured depths on the Daily Drilling Report
Items LW-410, LW-411 and LW-412 are charged for the metres drilled on an Operating day while the tool is in the hole, which are the metres logged.
Item RM-510 is charged for the metres drilled on an Operating day while the underreamer is in the hole, which are the metres reamed.
Gyro surveys, formation pressure points, wiper trips, back-reaming hours and clean-out runs are charged in the numbers recorded on the Daily Drilling Report for an Operating day.
The minimum in Clause 21 applies to each Operating day separately and is not averaged over a run.
Circulating hours are stated in whole hours, any part hour of thirty minutes or more counting as a whole hour.
Part 7 — Minimum hours DD-120: not less than 6 hours on an Operating day (Clause 21).
For a service charged by the hour, the first hour of each period in the hole is rig-up and is not a Chargeable Hour. The report states the hours run; the invoice charges one fewer.
Metres charged not exceeding the metres the report supports by more than 1 per cent are payable as charged. Metres exceeding that are payable at the figure the report supports.

discrepancies: Notes (ambiguities, not resolved): (1) The text does not say whether the 6-hour minimum (Cl.21, Sch 3 Part 7, P10) is applied before or after the one-hour rig-up deduction in 21A; the rule correctly leaves this open (Q4). (2) 21A speaks of 'the first hour of each period in the hole' but then 'The report states the hours run; the invoice charges one fewer' without saying whether 'one fewer' is per period or per report/day where a period spans several days. (3) Cl.21 says DD-120 is charged 'per circulating hour recorded', while 21A deducts the first hour; the two are reconciled only by reading 21A as the later, particular condition. (4) 'Part A depths' is Schedule 5 terminology (p24, not cited here); Cl.23 says only 'the measured depths on the Daily Drilling Report'. The validation arithmetic is consistent with the text: exactly +1% is 'not exceeding ... by more than 1 per cent' (payable as charged), +1.01% exceeds it (payable at the report figure); 7 hours run -> 6 charged. Parameter values match the print: '6 hours', 'the first hour', '1 per cent'.

quotes.text: A charge is stated in the unit Schedule 1 gives for the service, and in no other.

discrepancies: Note (not a discrepancy): Cl.35 states the requirement only; p8 gives no monetary consequence for a charge stated in another unit, so the validation's 'breach recorded; monetary remedy per Q11' correctly treats the remedy as open. The contract text on p8 neither imports nor refers to any clause of the CW contract.

quotes.text: This Contract is to be read with the instruments below, in the order issued. Each takes effect on its own effective date and governs services performed on or after it; nothing in an instrument reopens a service already charged at the rate then chargeable.

A rate stated in Schedule 1 is the rate chargeable only until an instrument substitutes another for it. Pricing a service therefore requires the date on which it was performed, not the date of the invoice.
DD-120 Rotary steerable system, circula hour 384.15 398.50 2025-07-01
Where a service is performed in a month later than the last month stated below, the rate last published applies until it is superseded.
December 2025 736.40

The rates below are substituted for the rates in Schedule 1 for services performed on or after the effective date stated against each. Services performed before that date are charged at the rate previously chargeable.

Item DD-120 (Rotary steerable system, circulating) is re-published monthly against the Steerable Tool Index (Gulf, per hour). The rate chargeable is the rate published for the calendar month in which the service was performed.

Where this instrument and an earlier instrument both state a rate or a discount for the same service, the later governs services performed on or after its effective date, and the earlier governs services performed before it.
Reference DDS-2025-118/A3. Issued 17 August 2026 and taking effect 1 February 2026.

Services performed on or after that date and already invoiced shall be re-priced at the substituted rates and the difference shown as a single adjustment on the first invoice submitted after the date of issue (Clause 36A).
DD-120 Rotary steerable system, circula hour 398.50 416.00 2026-02-01

discrepancies: Validation case 'DD-120 Apr-2026: 416.00 (A3) not 406.00 (S2)' is stated without the condition the text attaches to a backdated amendment. A3 (p42) was issued 17 August 2026 with effect from 1 February 2026 and says already-invoiced services are re-priced with 'the difference shown as a single adjustment on the first invoice submitted after the date of issue'; 36A (p35, not cited) adds that 'an invoice submitted before that date of issue was correct at the rate then in force' (and says 'on or after the date of issue', whereas A3 says 'after'), and the SoV (p37) says 'nothing in an instrument reopens a service already charged at the rate then chargeable'. So an April 2026 DD-120 invoice submitted before 17 August 2026 at the S2 rate of 406.00 was correct under the text; 416.00 governs only an invoice submitted on or after A3's issue, with earlier invoices corrected by the single adjustment. Ambiguity (not resolved): A3 governs over S2's monthly table only if 'the later' instrument means the later-issued one (SoV: 'in the order issued'); read by effective date, S2 (effective 2026-04-01) is later than A3 (effective 2026-02-01), and A3 does not mention the S2 monthly table. The other validation cases match the print: DD-120 384.15 up to 2025-06-30 and 398.50 from 2025-07-01 (S1); HC-601 in January 2026 carries December 2025's 736.40 under the 'rate last published applies' sentence of S1 1.2. Schedule 1 itself (named in the title) is not among the cited pages.

quotes.text: The services below are priced against the Rig Services Index, base 100.00 (Clause 17A). The rate stated in Schedule 1 for them is a base rate.
MW-310 MWD directional and gamma tool 2,245.85 day
HC-620 Drilling jar rental 539.65 day

The rate for a service listed in Schedule 2C is the base rate stated in Schedule 1 multiplied by the Rig Services Index published for the calendar month in which the service was performed and divided by the base index, rounded half to even. That figure is the rate for the purposes of Clause 17.

discrepancies: Note (ambiguity, not resolved): 17A says the indexed figure 'is the rate for the purposes of Clause 17'; on p6 Clause 17 is Rounding and the build-up is Clause 18. The rule's 'before the build-up' is a reading of that cross-reference (S2 2.2 and A2 2.3 likewise call the build-up 'the build-up required by Clause 17'). Arithmetic checked: 2,245.85 x 103.60 / 100.00 = 2,326.7006, which rounds to 2,326.70.

quotes.text: Where a step of the build-up in Clause 18 produces a fraction of a cent, the result of that step is rounded to the nearest cent before the next step is applied, and a result exactly half way between two cents is rounded to the even cent.

to which is applied, in this order and no other: first the hole section factor in Schedule 3 Part 1, where the service is section-rated; then the well class factor in Schedule 3 Part 2, where the service is class-rated; then the standby percentage in Schedule 3 Part 3, where the day is a Standby day. Each step is rounded under Clause 17.
On a Standby day a service is charged at the percentage of its operating rate stated in Schedule 3 Part 3.
Personnel are charged on a Standby day at the standby percentage for their position in Schedule 3 Part 3.
Section-rated services: DD-110, DD-120, PD-220, MW-310, RM-510, RM-511.
HPHT 1.325
Class-rated services: DD-120, PD-210, MW-310, MW-320, LW-410, LW-411, LW-412, LW-413.
DD-101 Directional driller, 24-hour coverage 80%
HC-620 Drilling jar rental 50%
The hole-section factor in Schedule 3 Part 1 is not applied on a day the rig is on Standby, the section not being drilled.

A discount of 4 per cent is allowed on the services listed below for services performed on or after 1 April 2026. The discount is applied to the rate, as the last factor in the build-up required by Clause 17 and before the rounding it requires.

A discount of 7 per cent is allowed on the services listed below for services performed on or after 1 July 2026. The discount is applied to the rate, as the last factor in the build-up required by Clause 17 and before the rounding it requires.

discrepancies: Notes (not discrepancies): (1) The two 'App B' validation figures were checked on Appendix B (p30, not in the cited pages): '03-Jun-2025 DD-101 12-1/4" Standby 2 1,477.88 2,955.76' and '04-Jun-2025 DD-120 12-1/4" Operating 18 509.00 9,162.00'; 1,847.35 x 0.80 = 1,477.88 and 384.15 x 1.00 (12-1/4") x 1.325 = 508.99875 -> 509.00, as stated. (2) 423 x 0.945 = 399.735 exactly; half to even gives 399.74 (binary float gives 399.73499999..., which would round to 399.73). 423.00 is the S2 DD-120 figure for July 2026 (p40); the case is arithmetic only. (3) Ambiguity: S2 2.2 and A2 2.3 place the discount in 'the build-up required by Clause 17', while on p6 the build-up is Clause 18 and Clause 17 is rounding. A2 describes its 7 per cent as 'the deepening of the Supplement No. 2 discount' and says the later instrument governs from its effective date, so 7 per cent replaces 4 per cent from 2026-07-01 rather than adding to it. (4) 17B (p35) also says the well-class factor is not applied to PD-210, although Sch 3 Part 2 lists PD-210 as class-rated; this rule does not rely on that sentence.
